text:
omar_cs: Customer (FintechX) seeing intermittent structured-output parse failures. They call our hosted API with json_mode=strict and ~2-3% of responses fail client-side with 'InvalidDocument: missing required field \"amount\" in item[4]'. Happens during high throughput bursts.

jess_devex: Can you paste a failing request_id and a minimal response sample? region? model?

omar_cs: request_id: req_2623456789_finX_01, region: us-west-2, model: gptx-redwood-1. Example request (trimmed):
```http
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...
Content-Type: application/json
{ "json_mode": "strict", "schema": { "orders": [{ "id": "string", "amount": "number", "meta": {"source": "string"} }] }, "input": "..." }
```
Customer's client logs show a parse error when streaming:
```
JSONParseError: Unexpected end of input while parsing object at item index 4
raw_chunk_before_error: '\n[{"id":"a1","amount":100},{"id":"a2","amount":200},{"id":"a3","amount":150}, {"id":"a4","am'
```
You can see the stream got cut inside the key name 'amount'. The model continuation later sends the rest, but the strict streaming parser errors out when that chunk boundary arrives.

andrew_sre: Thanks — that looks like a stream-chunking boundary problem. We had a recent change that increased token aggregation per frame for throughput; it can split a JSON token mid-key in edge cases. Streaming clients that assume frames contain whole syntactic units will break.

ryan_runtime: Repro steps I ran locally:
1) curl -N to enable streaming
2) send a large batch to force >8KB output
3) observe chunks where arrays/items are split mid-object
Example server-side snippet we captured:
```
...
{"id":"a3","amount":150}, {"id":"a4","am
```
then next chunk:
```
ount":175,"meta":{"source":"user"}} ,{"id":"a5","amount":90}]
```
So the client's strict per-chunk parser throws.

jess_devex: Does the client parser assume each chunk == full JSON document? Many SDKs incrementally parse across chunks; but some naive parsers don't. Is this new behavior after the perf change?

ryan_runtime: Yes, regression after the throughput aggregation change. Patch in review to avoid splitting on UTF-8 codepoint boundaries inside tokens and to prefer chunk boundaries at JSON structural tokens when possible. Not a full fix for all sizes, but will reduce incidents.

omar_cs: Customer also sees extra unexpected keys occasionally (e.g., 'temp_meta') that cause strict schema validation to fail. Sample snippet: 
```json
{"id":"a6","amount":120,"temp_meta":"x"}
```
They expect exact-schema enforcement and fail on extra fields.

andrew_sre: Two orthogonal issues: (1) chunk splitting leads to parse errors; (2) schema drift / extra keys cause strict validation fails. For (2) we should confirm whether those keys come from post-processing or from a model hallucination.

ryan_runtime: I grepped the runtime logs for req_2623456789_finX_01 and saw a post-filter step that injects metadata in rare upstream branches (legacy telemetry hook) — it can add temp_meta when a debug flag was set. That explains extra keys. I will push a fix to disable that hook by default.

lina_pm: This is affecting one paying customer with retries, so billing spike and latency complaints are starting. Can SRE/Runtime prioritize a hotfix and we coordinate rollback if needed? Also need a customer-facing mitigation we can share.

andrew_sre: Hotfix plan: (a) disable telemetry injection hook (rollback flag) — low risk, (b) revert aggregation-aggressive chunking to previous policy for hosted for 24h while we test improved boundaries, (c) add server-side fallback: if json_mode=strict and the stream parser hits an incomplete chunk, queue the remainder until full object detected instead of failing the request. We can do (a)+(b) in next 30m. (c) is a follow-up.

jess_devex: Recommended customer mitigation to share now: 1) switch to json_mode=permissive (if acceptable) to ignore extra keys and tolerate partial ordering, 2) or buffer stream client-side and parse across chunks (most SDKs already do this), 3) if they can't, ask them to reduce batch output size or max_tokens to avoid chunk splits. Provide example code for buffering: 
```js
let buffer = '';
response.on('data', chunk => {
  buffer += chunk.toString();
  try { const doc = JSON.parse(buffer); handle(doc); buffer = ''; } catch (e) { /* wait for more */ }
});
```
Note: naive JSON.parse approach only works if responses are single JSON docs; for streaming arrays you need a streaming parser (clarinet/sax-like).

omar_cs: I relayed that. Customer requested ETA.

andrew_sre: ETA: disable telemetry hook in 20m, revert chunking policy in 45m, monitor error rate and p99 latency. If error rate doesn't drop, escalate to full rollback. I'll post deploy ids here.

buildbot: deploy/rollout:4692 to us-west-2 queued by ryant; telemetry-hook-flag=false rolled out to 8/10 hosts; chunking-policy reverted on canary hosts.

ryan_runtime: I'll open a follow-up ticket to add robust JSON streaming reassembly in the runtime when json_mode=strict is requested and to add a lint that prevents telemetry hook from touching payload objects.

lina_pm: Thanks. Please DM me updates and I'll craft a customer status note.

omar_cs: Thanks team — I'll update customer with the mitigation steps and ETA. :thumbsup:
